say.en: A family can have 2 or 3 children, never 2.5. But a child can be 120.6 centimetres tall. What is the difference? In this lesson: Define a variable.
Distinguish continuous and discrete variables.

body.en: A *variable* is a characteristic that changes from one unit to another and can be measured, such as income, age or marks. Variables are of two kinds: continuous and discrete.
body.kn: ಒಂದು ಘಟಕದಿಂದ ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಬದಲಾಗುವ, ಅಳೆಯಬಹುದಾದ ಲಕ್ಷಣ ಚರಾಂಶ. ಇದು ನಿರಂತರ ಅಥವಾ ವಿಚ್ಛಿನ್ನ ಆಗಿರಬಹುದು.

narration.en: A discrete variable jumps in whole steps: a family has 2 or 3 children, never 2.5. A continuous variable can take any value in a range: a height can be 162.3 or 162.35 cm. Move both sliders and watch how the marker moves. Can the children marker stop between two dots? Name two more variables of each kind from your own class.

title.en: On the board: Continuous or discrete?

say.en: A continuous variable can take any value in a range, even fractions, like height.
Every point on the line is possible: 152.4 cm, 157.25 cm.
A discrete variable jumps from one value to the next, like the number of children.
There is nothing between 2 and 3 children. Values in between are impossible.

explanation.en: A continuous variable can take fractional values (1.62 m, 36.4 °C). A discrete variable jumps between separate values: a family cannot have 2.5 children.

body.en: A *continuous* variable can take any value in a range, including fractions: height, weight, time, temperature. A discrete variable takes only certain values, usually whole numbers, and jumps from one value to the next: number of children, number of cars, number of workers.
body.kn: ನಿರಂತರ ಚರಾಂಶ ಒಂದು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಯ ಯಾವುದೇ ಮೌಲ್ಯ ಪಡೆಯಬಹುದು. ವಿಚ್ಛಿನ್ನ ಚರಾಂಶ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಮೌಲ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ, ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಪೂರ್ಣಾಂಕಗಳನ್ನು ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Discrete: counted (children, cars, rooms).

problem.en: Classify: (i) area of farms in hectares, (ii) number of trees in a garden, (iii) daily rainfall in mm, (iv) number of goals scored.

steps.en: (i) Area can be any fraction of a hectare: continuous.
(ii) Trees are counted in whole numbers: discrete.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Classify: (i) area of farms in hectares, (ii) number of trees in a garden, (iii) daily rainfall in mm, (iv) number of goals scored.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Classify: i area of farms in hectares, ii number of trees in a garden, iii daily rainfall in mm, iv number of goals scored.
i Area can be any fraction of a hectare: continuous.
ii Trees are counted in whole numbers: discrete.
iii Rainfall can be 12.4 millimetres: continuous.
iv Goals are whole numbers: discrete.
So the answer is Continuous: i, iii; Discrete: ii, iv.

body.en: If you measure it with a scale, clock or weighing machine, it is continuous. If you count it on your fingers, it is discrete.

narration.en: Measure or count?. If you measure it with a scale, clock or weighing machine, it is continuous. If you count it on your fingers, it is discrete.

say.en: Measure or count?. If you measure it with a scale, clock or weighing machine, it is continuous. If you count it on your fingers, it is discrete.
